key_insight: MRI appearance variability can be disentangled into anatomy and acquisition effects by jointly learning from images and DICOM metadata.
clinical_relevance: This could improve MRI harmonisation, robustness across scanners/sites, and detection of image–metadata mismatches in clinical workflows.
method: Learned representations from large-scale brain MRI plus DICOM metadata
Separated anatomy-preserving features from contrast/acquisition features
Built a harmonisation model conditioned on image or acquisition metadata
evidence_signal: The study used large-scale clinical brain MRI data and reports that the learned representations separated structure from contrast, organised heterogeneous acquisitions, and detected image–metadata inconsistencies.
watch_item: Performance may depend on metadata quality and consistent DICOM availability, so real-world deployment needs careful auditing and validation.
paper_title: Metadata Supervised MRI Representations for Modelling and Controlling Acquisition Variability
